The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: Turning on a feature switch made shoppers' account pages work out their average spend per item this month, and that sum fails by dividing by zero, likely for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 8m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 38.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 5,182.30 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #530 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load while monthly-spend-feature was on
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 02:14 to 02:22 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 02:39:19 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 02:20:43 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 02:14 UTC and was back to normal at 02:22 UTC, 8 minutes later. 26.3% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 38.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 5,182.30 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Turning on a feature switch made shoppers' account pages work out their average spend per item this month, and that sum fails by dividing by zero, likely for shoppers who have bought nothing this month. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #530, for a person to review and merge. If monthly-spend-feature is switched on again before a fix is in place, account pages could fail again, likely for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

Impact
8m 0s - onset until back to normal
38.5% - peak error rate
2,526 - requests failed
1.0% to 26.3% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
5,182.30 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend figure goes through average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total by the number of purchases made this month and has no case for a shopper who bought nothing this month. For such a shopper the number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and the page request fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed with errors, and the account page error rate stayed high minute after minute.
  Evidence:
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 02:14–02:20
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 9 occurrences in 9 minutes, 02:12–02:20; # was 0.50% to 38.50%, typically 28.00%, highest at 02:15
why 1 The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 At 02:14:28 UTC the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on. Before that, its evaluations came back all off. In the minute it was switched they were split, and after that they were all on. The division-by-zero errors began in the minute the flag was switched.
  Evidence:
    P1 02:14:28 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 2 occurrences in 2 minutes, 02:12–02:13
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 98 / on 102 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 02:14
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:15–02:20
    G5309
  Ruled out:
    The switch-on of the flag an-unrelated-feature at 02:20:18 UTC. It came after the onset at 02:14 UTC, by which time the account page errors were already high.
      P2 02:20:18 UTC flag toggle an-unrelated-feature by admin: feature flag an-unrelated-feature was switched on
      T5 02:20:55 Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 02:14
      Gbac1
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 02:15; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change.
      T7
      T8
why 3 With the flag on, the account page divides the month's spend by the number of purchases made this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought nothing this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    G5309
Contributing factors
- No check was seen before monthly-spend-feature was switched on in production that ran the flag-on code path for a shopper with no purchases this month. (AI-3)
- The flag went from off for all evaluations to on for all evaluations straight away. No staged rollout to a small share of shoppers, and nothing that stops a rollout on rising errors, was seen. (AI-4)
- An error while working out the spend summary failed the whole account page request rather than only leaving out that figure. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 02:14:28 UTC. That enabled a code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate stepped from about 1% to about 30%. No deployment was involved. | 0.95 | confirmed

Trigger
monthly-spend-feature flag went from OFF to ON at 02:14:28 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 02:21:09 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 02:24:45 | Proposed a fix: PR #530 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 02:14 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 02:20:18 UTC, 6 minutes 18 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #530 | open
AI-3 | Require tests that run a feature flag's on path to pass before that flag can be switched on in production for io-shop. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Roll out feature flag changes on io-shop to a small share of traffic first, and stop the rollout automatically when the error rate rises. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Make the account page load without the spend summary when the summary fails, rather than failing the whole request. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page so that a person is paged when it fires. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Keep monthly-spend-feature off until a fix for the spend summary is merged and deployed. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 41 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 41 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 2 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:20:59.
- 51 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 4 minutes 27 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #530.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was called to the incident.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)

T17 | 02:21:17 |  | Mitigation Agent Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 02:22 - up to 170s

Response effort
none - engineer time
130,949 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/0ea491b5-f9ef-4ff6-b1f6-a0d36dc2c5f9
The fix it proposed: PR #530 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/530) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | 02:14:28 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
P2 | 02:20:18 UTC flag toggle an-unrelated-feature by admin: feature flag an-unrelated-feature was switched on
Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G7e5d | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 2 occurrences in 2 minutes, 02:12–02:13
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 3 occurrences in 2 minutes, 02:12–02:13
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 9 occurrences in 9 minutes, 02:12–02:20; # was 0.50% to 38.50%, typically 28.00%, highest at 02:15
G971b | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 98 / on 102 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 02:14
G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 02:14–02:20
Gce95 | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:15–02:20
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py divides account.total_this_month_cents by len(bought_this_month), the number of purchases flagged in_current_month. Most shoppers have bought before but not this month. For them that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. That is the line the incident log names (spend_summary.py:47). Turning on monthly-spend-feature sent the account page's figure through this function, and every request for such a shopper failed.

The flag was what triggered the incident, but the fault is in the code: the function has no answer for the normal case of a shopper who has bought nothing this month. With the fix, when there are no purchases this month the function returns 0, because a shopper with no purchases this month has spent nothing this month. Otherwise it divides as before. Shoppers who did buy this month get the same result as before.

Other code is unchanged. With the flag off, render_spend_summary still uses average_spend_per_item, and that function still raises for an account with no purchases at all. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py and tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py expect that error, and that error is the only case the line-number test in test_account_page.py checks. Nothing in this change catches errors.

The tests: the new cases in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py call average_spend_per_item_this_month and render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True) for a shopper whose purchases all fall outside the current month, and assert 0. Against the current code both would raise ZeroDivisionError.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, io-shop's account pages failed to load for some shoppers, likely those who had bought nothing this month. It started when a feature switch was turned on. The switch made account pages work out each shopper's average spend per item this month, and that sum fails because it divides by zero. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, so no on-call staff were called in. Argus ended the incident by turning off the feature switch, monthly-spend-feature. That change is confirmed and still in place. Argus has also proposed a fix in PR #530. It is open as a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
